story.title: Yayoi Kusama, Renowned Japanese Artist, Passes Away at 97
story.summary: Yayoi Kusama, the celebrated Japanese artist known for her iconic polka dot designs and immersive installations, has died at the age of 97. Her passing occurred on August 14, 2026, in a Tokyo hospital, as confirmed by her company. Kusama's work, which spanned several decades, has left a significant impact on contemporary art, attracting global audiences and prompting widespread tributes.

explore_lenses.label: Why does Kusama’s death matter to art audiences?
explore_lenses.title: A legacy across art forms and public institutions
explore_lenses.summary: Kusama’s importance extends beyond her recognizable dots: museums describe a practice that connected painting, sculpture, performance, fashion, literature and immersive installations, helping make participatory art a major public draw.

claims.text: Museum Ludwig’s 2026 retrospective assembled more than 300 works across painting, drawing, sculpture, installation, fashion, performance and literature, illustrating the range of Kusama’s practice.
The Smithsonian’s Hirshhorn identifies her 1965 Infinity Mirror Room—Phalli’s Field as a breakthrough that transformed repeated forms from earlier works into a perceptual, participatory experience.

Museum Ludwig says Kusama’s dots, pumpkins and Infinity Mirror Rooms became widely reproduced social-media trademarks; this is the museum’s explanation for her unusually broad contemporary visibility.

explore_lenses.label: How did Kusama build such a long career?
explore_lenses.title: She kept expanding a consistent visual language
explore_lenses.summary: Her career combined a stable set of motifs—dots, nets, repetition and infinity—with shifts between media and decades of new production, rather than relying solely on earlier landmark works.

claims.text: Kusama’s official biography says she moved to the United States in 1957, developed net paintings, soft sculptures and mirror-and-light installations in New York, and returned to Japan in 1973, where she resumed work in literature, sculpture and the Infinity Mirror Room series.
Her official biography states that she produced roughly 900 paintings in the My Eternal Soul series from 2009 to 2021 and began Every Day I Pray for Love in 2021.
The artist’s studio said Kusama continued painting until her final days and intended to keep advancing themes it described as “forever love” and “eternal soul.”

explore_lenses.label: What happens next for her exhibitions and museum?
explore_lenses.title: Scheduled shows and institutional programming continue
explore_lenses.summary: At least two Kusama-related exhibition programs were publicly scheduled before or on the day her death was announced, while decisions about longer-term stewardship of her estate and future production have not been detailed publicly in the consulted materials.

claims.text: Ota Fine Arts, which represented Kusama, announced that the traveling retrospective is scheduled to open at Amsterdam’s Stedelijk Museum on September 11, 2026.
Fondation Beyeler describes the Stedelijk presentation, scheduled for September 11, 2026 through January 17, 2027, as part of a jointly organized exhibition sequence with Beyeler and Museum Ludwig.

The Yayoi Kusama Museum’s official ticketing page says it will close from August 31 to October 7, 2026 to prepare for an upcoming exhibition; its Japanese upcoming-exhibitions page lists dates from October 8, 2026 to January 31, 2027.

story_report.summary: Yayoi Kusama, the Japanese artist whose polka dots and immersive installations drew audiences worldwide, died in Tokyo on August 14 at age 97. Her studio did not disclose a cause of death. Kusama’s work ranged across painting, sculpture, installations, fashion, performance and literature, while her Infinity Mirror Rooms became a defining participatory form. Exhibitions of her work are still scheduled in Europe and Japan, extending a public presence built over decades of experimentation and prolific late-career painting.

sections.heading: Kusama’s Career Crossed Media and Continents
sections.body: Kusama moved to the United States in 1957 and, in New York, developed net paintings, soft sculptures, and mirror-and-light installations, according to her official biography. After returning to Japan in 1973, she resumed work in literature, sculpture and the Infinity Mirror Room series. Her output remained extensive in later years: the biography says she made roughly 900 paintings in the My Eternal Soul series between 2009 and 2021, then began Every Day I Pray for Love in 2021.

sections.heading: Kusama’s Mirror Rooms Expanded Participation
sections.body: The Hirshhorn describes Kusama’s 1965 Infinity Mirror Room—Phalli’s Field as a breakthrough that turned repeated forms from her earlier work into a perceptual and participatory experience. A 2026 Museum Ludwig retrospective assembled more than 300 works in painting, drawing, sculpture, installation, fashion, performance and literature. Museum Ludwig attributes Kusama’s unusually broad contemporary visibility in part to the widespread reproduction of her dots, pumpkins and Infinity Mirror Rooms as social-media trademarks.

sections.heading: Kusama Exhibitions Remain on Schedule
sections.body: Ota Fine Arts, which represented Kusama, said a traveling retrospective is scheduled to open at Amsterdam’s Stedelijk Museum on September 11, 2026. Fondation Beyeler lists the Stedelijk presentation, running through January 17, 2027, as part of a jointly organized sequence with Beyeler and Museum Ludwig. In Tokyo, the Yayoi Kusama Museum says it will close from August 31 to October 7 to prepare an exhibition listed to run from October 8 through January 31, 2027.

related_stories.summary: King Harald of Norway is reported to be in an 'extremely serious' condition in the hospital, prompting family members to gather at his bedside. As news of his health deteriorating spreads, hundreds of Norwegians have gathered outside the Royal Palace in Oslo, laying flowers in a show of support for the 89-year-old monarch.

related_stories.title: Russian Drone Strikes Hit Multiple Ukrainian Cities, Causing Casualties and Fires
related_stories.summary: Overnight on August 27, Russian drone strikes targeted nine Ukrainian cities, including Sumy and Odesa, resulting in at least one death and seven injuries, according to regional authorities. The attacks have ignited fires across these areas, marking a significant escalation in hostilities.

related_stories.title: UEFA Initiates Criminal Proceedings Against Gianni Infantino Over World Cup Stake Sale
related_stories.summary: UEFA is preparing to file a criminal complaint in Swiss courts against FIFA President Gianni Infantino. The complaint arises from Infantino's failed attempt to sell a stake in World Cup revenues to private investors for $4.2 billion, which UEFA lawyers described as a 'fraudulently off-market price.'
